references.text: God made a covenant with Abraham, promising to give his descendants the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.
God established an eternal covenant with Abraham and his descendants, promising to give them the land of Canaan.
God confirmed the covenant with Isaac and promised to bless him and his descendants because of Abraham.
God confirmed the covenant with Jacob and promised him the land and numerous descendants.
God promised Jacob that He would make him into a great nation in Egypt and bring his descendants back to the promised land.
When God revealed Himself to Moses, He identified as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God said that He had heard the cries of the Israelites and remembered His covenant.
God promised to remember His covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, and to remember the land.
God is merciful and will not forget the covenant He made with the fathers.
Nehemiah reminds us that God chose Abraham and made a covenant with him to give the land to his descendants.
God remembers His covenant forever, the covenant He made with Abraham, confirmed for Isaac, and established for Jacob.
God looked upon His people in their distress, heard their cry, and remembered His covenant with them.
Zechariah praises God for showing mercy to the fathers and remembering His holy covenant, the oath He swore to Abraham.
Stephen recounts that as the time for the fulfillment of the promise drew near, the people grew in Egypt.
Both verses demonstrate that God's intervention and grace toward a suffering people are directly rooted in His eternal covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The psalm theologically confirms that God's salvation history with Israel is founded on the same covenant with Abraham and Isaac that triggers Moses' call.
The shared title 'God of the Fathers' links together God's identity as the foundation for both Moses' authority and His merciful intervention in Egypt.
Direct narrative and theological connection: Chapter 2 explains *why* God intervenes (the covenant), while chapter 3 describes *how* He reveals Himself as the God of the Fathers to carry it out.
